name: Pårte-Kvikkjokk
estimatedTime: 6-8 hours per STF; 5-8 hours per Naturkartan
difficulty: Official text describes mostly easy montane-forest walking with rocky sections; field reports consistently warn the section becomes much harder in wet weather because of mud, slippery rock/root footing, waterlogged trail and stream-like slopes.
routeType: point-to-point mountain-forest section with road/bus access at Kvikkjokk and no boat crossing on this section

officialSources.name: STF Kungsleden Saltoluokta-Kvikkjokk route page
officialSources.evidence: Identifies stage 4 as STF Pårte Mountain Cabin to STF Kvikkjokk Mountain Station, 17 km and 6-8 hours. Describes dense forest, Tjåltajåkkå bridge, rougher/rockier trail after the bridge, Lake Stuor Tata/Dáhta context and final slopes that can become stream-like after prolonged rain.

officialSources.name: Naturkartan BD66 Pårte-Kvikkjokk
officialSources.evidence: Official route page/title Pårte-Kvikkjokk, Kungsleden / The King's Trail, with 17.0 km and 5-8 hours. Describes montane forest, rocky sections, plankways, Lake Stuor Dáhta/Stuor Tata, Tingstallstenen/Diggehájkgallo, final gravel road and risk that northbound hikers miss the turn off the road.

wildCamping.summary: Naturkartan says tent pitches exist along the whole section. Field reports mention Pårte lakeshore, stream/bridge areas and more campsites closer to Kvikkjokk, but exact informal camp/fire POIs are mostly OSM-only and should remain pending unless informal POIs are in scope.
caveats: Wet/rooty forest and waterlogged ground can limit usable tent sites in rain.
Kvikkjokk-Kabla reserve allows camping, but selected-site rules and reindeer/grazing sensitivity still matter.
Near Pårte, Sarek/Laponia boundary uncertainty means campsite rules should be checked with GIS before applying national-park-specific restrictions.

fire.summary: Kvikkjokk-Kabla and Kamajokk reserve pages allow fires under applicable rules, but fire bans override this and Länsstyrelsen general guidance favors established fireplaces. OSM-only firepits should remain pending until verified or accepted as informal POIs.
rules: Check Länsstyrelsen/Krisinformation/Brandrisk Ute immediately before lighting any fire.
Do not damage plant/animal life or cut/remove trees/windfalls except where specific reserve allowances and restrictions permit.
Sarek/Laponia rules may apply near Pårte depending on exact boundary; use only loose ground wood where allowed.

protectedAreas.name: Sarek National Park / Laponia boundary zone near Pårte
protectedAreas.evidence: Pårte is a gateway/starting point for Sarek and the previous stage traverses Sarek; Laponia says Bårdde/Pårte cabins are just outside Sarek National Park and Laponia World Heritage Area.
protectedAreas.caveat: Exact cabin-to-boundary point and campsite-specific rule side require GIS overlay before normalized rules import.

protectedAreas.name: Kvikkjokk-Kabla fjällurskog Nature Reserve and Natura 2000
protectedAreas.evidence: Länsstyrelsen and Naturvårdsverket documentation identify the Kvikkjokk side as within/adjacent to Kvikkjokk-Kabla fjällurskog, protected as both nature reserve and Natura 2000, bordering Sarek to the north.
protectedAreas.caveat: Exact route-overlap should be verified using selected geometry and official protected-area layers.

reserveRules: Kvikkjokk-Kabla allows camping, hiking, fires, berry/mushroom picking, snowmobile use on well snow-covered ground and fishing/hunting under applicable laws.
Forestry is prohibited; cutting/removing trees or windfalls needs permission, with limited on-site firewood allowance excluding standing dead pine/spruce.
sarekLaponiaRules: Hunting and fishing are prohibited in national parks.
Drones/flight below 2,000 ft and takeoff/landing require permission according to Laponia guidance used by rules lane.
Watercraft, cycling and horses are prohibited in Sarek.
Damaging vegetation, soil, stone or wildlife is prohibited.
Camping for a day or so and fires with loose ground wood are allowed subject to fire bans.
Dogs are generally prohibited in Laponia national parks, but leashed dogs are allowed January 1-April 30 and leashed dogs are allowed year-round on Kungsleden.

fireBans.summary: Protected-area fire permissions do not override fire bans. Check current Länsstyrelsen/Krisinformation/Brandrisk Ute before any fire.

fishingHunting.summary: For non-Sarek waters, use 2026 Jokkmokk/Norrbotten fjällfiske rules and map appendices; hunting periods in Kvikkjokk-Kabla remain an awareness/currentness open question.

reindeer.summary: Sarek is core reindeer-herding land and Kvikkjokk-Kabla is important grazing land, especially spring/autumn. Do not disturb herds; detour or wait.

currentNotices: Länsstyrelsen 2026-04-22 notice: trail checks stopped because spring warmth made snow/ice unreliable; ice crossings may be unsafe or impossible.
Länsstyrelsen 2026-03-27 notice: changed snow/ice conditions across the county, including weak ice, open water and variable snow depth.
No Pårte-Kvikkjokk-specific bridge or closure notice was found on the current notice index at access date 2026-04-29.

Laponia current info says Sarek/Badjelánnda bridges were lifted for winter 2025/2026 and summer bridges are normally placed around the last week of June and removed mid-September; mainly relevant for Sarek side trips rather than the main Pårte-Kvikkjokk stage.
serviceDates: STF Kvikkjokk summer hours shown as 08:00-21:00; restaurant, shop, cafe, guest kitchen, sauna, Wi-Fi and equipment rental listed.
STF Kvikkjokk page warns of late-winter 2026 renovation: limited self-catering rooms, restaurant closed, cafe open and shop limited.
routeHazards: Rough rocky trail after Tjåltajåkka bridge.
Slopes around Tingstallstenen can become stream-like after prolonged rain.
High flows can rise quickly after rain/snowmelt.
Wet weather can create mud, waterlogged trail and slippery rock/root travel.
Mosquito risk is high in warm/humid forest, especially when stopping.

conditionReports.summary: Reviews are mixed but consistently show wet weather changes the section: northbound from Kvikkjokk can have a hard ascent with full pack, rocky/tough terrain, wet/slippery/muddy trail after rain and occasionally good conditions.

Reports lakeside miles with open views, tricky reindeer-fence crawl-through, many campsites closer to Kvikkjokk, merge with ATV/gravel track into town and weaker STF Kvikkjokk shop resupply than Saltoluokta.
First forest had mosquitoes basically everywhere; after about two hours route reached lakes with rocky/uneven path near water; thunderstorm arrived near Pårte; author camped at Pårte lakeshore.

Describes humid forest, high mosquitoes, wet/muddy trail, later deep mud, unstable rocks and water; notes good bridges, lunch/water spots, a dedicated campsite with drop toilets by a fast river/wooden bridge and waterlogged stretches near Kvikkjokk.

Recorded distances/times include 16.7 km / 7 h 13 min northbound and 9.95 mi / 5 h 23 min southbound; a 2025 comment warns heavy rain made it slippery, much slower and not family-friendly in those conditions.

conditionReports.source: Reboot Life and PreTrek older reports
conditionReports.summary: Describe very rocky/wet trail, poor-condition forest trail, feet constantly underwater after drizzle, slippery/muddy footing and heavier crowding around Pårte/Kvikkjokk.
Calls Pårte-Kvikkjokk rough/rocky and possibly among the worst northern Kungsleden sections, with small hills and river crossings making it more strenuous than the elevation profile suggests.
